top.title: Inside Week 10 of CIAC football: Return tickets, ticking clocks and the unbeatens
top.description: Berlin's Chace Hrubiec (12) drops back for a pass during their game against Platt at Falcon Field in Meriden Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) It's almost that time. Playoff football is brewing, Thanksgiving is less than two weeks away, and numerous teams are on the edge of either clinching a spot in the tournaments or falling short of the postseason. An analysis of the field by GametimeCT had 11 teams unofficially clinching playoff berths heading into Week 10. That group featured some recent champions, such as Hand (2023 and 2025), Masuk (2024), Ansonia (2024), and Staples (2023). But there's plenty of room for newcomers. Of the 48 playoff spots, there are 20 teams that did not play in last year's tournaments that are inside the playoff bubble after Friday's games. Several of those teams have not appeared in the postseason in more than a decade, and one has never gone to the dance: Lewis Mills . Lewis Mills is in its 16th season as a program and now co-ops with Wolcott Tech , ranking sixth in Class L with a 6-2 record. Lyman Hall (M) and Plainville (SS) have both unofficially clinched berths in the playoffs. For Lyman Hall (7-2), it's the first bid since 2010, and for Plainville (9-0), it's the first since 2019. Pomperaug (8-1) is third in Class MM and is closing in on its first playoff berth since 2009, when it was runner-up in Class L. Xavier 's last trip to the playoffs resulted in a Class LL-Small championship in 2014. The Falcons (6-2) are seventh in Class MM. And one of the brightest stories in CIAC football this season, Simsbury , has gone from four wins in the last three years combined, to eight wins and a possible tournament berth. The Trojans are ranked fourth in Class L and should they qualify, it would be their first playoff appearance since 2019. The clock's ticking One of the many teams in need of a big win in Week 10 was defending Class M champion Berlin , which had taken a tough loss against Enfield in its most recent game. They got that bounce-back win by going back to the "old Berlin way." Berlin controlled the ball, the clock, and the game while rolling to a 26-0 win over Platt Thursday night in Meriden. Berlin had possession for 38 of 48 minutes and ran 51 plays to Platt's 20. "We had a horrible night versus Enfield. We didn't compete and we had to go to school the next day and it was a horrible feeling," Berlin coach John Capodice told GametimeCT's Bryant Carpenter. "We said, 'We've got to change this really, really quick. The clock's ticking. If you want to go into the playoffs and you want to be a quality football team, we had to go back to the old Berlin way, and that's competing for four quarters." By kicking it up a notch, Berlin improved to 6-3 and is in seventh place in the Class SS standings with one game remaining. It hosts Middletown (7-2) at 6:30 p.m., Friday. top.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
top.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra. “We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said. Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria. top.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
top.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. top.title: Aaron Wise Locks In New Titleist Driver For 2026 Season
top.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Aaron Wise has finalized his equipment setup for the late 2026 season, swapping in a new driver and wedge configuration. GolfWRX reported on November 14 that he is rolling with a Titleist GTS3 driver set at 10 degrees with a SureFit D1 setting. The shaft choice remains a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, a staple for players seeking stability off the tee. This specific combination suggests a focus on consistency as the PGA Tour moves through its fall schedule. Wise keeps his 3-wood from TaylorMade, utilizing a Qi4D model at 15 degrees paired with a heavier Fujikura Ventus Black 8 TX shaft. The hybrid slot features a TaylorMade SIM2 Max at 19 degrees, loaded with a Project X HZRDUS Black 6.5 100G shaft. His iron set consists of Titleist T100 models from 4 through PW, all fitted with True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. The wedges show the most significant change, with a Titleist Vokey Design SM11 52-12F bent to 51 degrees and a 56-08M adjusted to 55.5 degrees, alongside a Titleist Vokey Design WedgeWorks 60-L. All wedges carry True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. Short Game and Putter Selection The putter remains a TaylorMade Corza Ghost, a design that offers a clean look for alignment. GolfWRX confirmed the grip choice across the bag is the Golf Pride Tour Velvet Cord, providing a secure hold in varying weather conditions. The ball selection stays with the Titleist Pro V1, a standard for players prioritizing spin control on approach shots. These details were posted on Saturday, November 14, reflecting the current state of Wise’s bag as he prepares for upcoming events. What the Changes Mean Wise adjusted his wedge lofts to improve trajectory control around the greens. Bending the 52-degree wedge down to 51 and the 56-degree to 55.5 allows for tighter gapping between the pitching wedge and the sand wedge. The retention of the SIM2 Max hybrid suggests he still values the forgiveness of that club head, even as driver technology evolves. Sticking with the T100 irons shows confidence in the blade-like feel of the set, which demands solid contact but offers superior workability. The Fujikura Ventus Black shaft in the driver continues to be a top choice for the tour. Its stiffness profile helps manage face rotation, which is critical for maintaining accuracy. Wise’s setup aligns with many competitors who favor a high-launch, low-spin driver ball flight. The use of the Corza Ghost putter provides a counterbalance feel that can smooth out the stroke for players with a slight arc. Every component in this bag serves a specific purpose for a player competing at the highest level. Upcoming Schedule Context With the equipment list confirmed, Wise heads into the final stretch of the fall series. The focus now shifts to how these clubs perform under tournament pressure and varying course conditions. GolfWRX noted that more photos of the setup are available for fans to review.

top.title: Khamzat Chimaev blanks Chris Weidman with tech fall victory in RAF Abu Dhabi main event
top.description: Khamzat Chimaev put on another dominant performance to blank UFC Hall of Famer Chris Weidman in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event. Originally scheduled to face Colby Covington on Saturday, Chimaev accepted Weidman as a late notice replacement and showed why he’s such a danger on the wrestling mats. Chimaev poured on the offense and ultimately won off a challenge being denied after he used a four-point score that Weidman’s team didn’t agree with. The challenge was shut down and that gave Chimaev the clinching point to go up 10-0 and end the match by technical fall. “it feels good, it feels amazing,” Chimaev said about his win. “Anyone who wants to wrestle or fight, grapple, it doesn’t matter. I’m always ready.” Chimaev started strong and went up 5-0 in the first period after a takedown and turns on Weidman. To his credit, Weidman made Chimaev work for every position as he stayed in the match going into the second period. Weidman tried a slick move on the restart as he went for a slide by but Chimaev reversed positions for a four point score. That led to Weidman issuing challenge but that was denied giving Chimaev another point for the 10-0 technical fall victory. Chimaev has been unstoppable since arriving in RAF and it’s tough to believe the promotion won’t work tirelessly to rebook that match against Covington once he’s healthy enough to compete again.

Chimaev was originally expected to face former UFC welterweight contender Colby Covington in the RAF Abu Dhabi headliner before “Chaos” withdrew due to an undisclosed injury . top.title: Marlins Hit Coach Swap Ignores Real Progress Made In 2026
top.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports The Miami Marlins made a strange call by letting go of hitting coach Pedro Guerrero. Team president Peter Bendix announced the decision after the season ended. The front office claims they need a “new voice in the hitting space,” per reports. This reasoning does not hold up when looking at the actual numbers from the field. Guerrero Built a Real Foundation Guerrero left behind a lineup that actually improved. In 2024, the team finished 27th in runs and home runs. By 2025, they jumped to 18th in runs and 23rd in home runs. The offense also climbed to sixth in on-base percentage last year. Young players like Otto Lopez had a breakout All-Star campaign under his watch. Lopez led the majors with 191 base hits in 2026. Xavier Edwards and Kyle Stowers also developed well during this time. The stats show a clear upward trend that took two years to build. Lawson Has a Rocky History Hiring Dillon Lawson to replace Guerrero feels like a step backward. Lawson was fired mid-season by the New York Yankees in 2023. His time with the Red Sox also ended quickly after just over one year. The Boston team started 10-17 before he was let go. Even Aaron Judge struggled with a career-low bWAR of 4.6 in 2023 while working with Lawson. The Marlins are trading a coach who fixed their offense for one with a poor track record. Trade Talks and Roster Moves While the coaching staff changes, the front office is also eyeing trades. The Seattle Times reported that the Mariners asked about Otto Lopez. A lockout likely begins on Dec. 1, and they are also seeking pitching assistance. The plan is to make offers for pitchers before the work stoppage starts. With pitcher Bradley Blalock released, the Marlins roster now holds 35 players on their 40-man list.

top.description: UEFA Nations League: Arsenal-linked Nusa scores his tenth Norway goal, Orban set for early Leipzig return due to suspension Antonio Nusa scored his tenth Norway goal in their 3-1 victory over Wales in Oslo. The RB Leipzig winger broke the deadlock at the hour mark before ex-Borussia Dortmund striker Erling Haaland avoided what would have been a three-game scoreless run for the first time since March 2024 by netting the third from the penalty spot. The sought-after Leipzig attacker had a goal or an assist for his club in each of the last five games before the international break. Recent reports suggest Premier League champions Arsenal would go all in for him in January. Nusa's Norway are now level on points with Denmark, who will face Group A4 leaders Portugal later tonight. Fellow RB Leipzig man Willi Orban helped Hungary to a 2-0 victory away at out-of-sorts Georgia. The result put Hungary top of their group in League B before Northern Ireland's game against Ukraine. Köln's defender Luka Lochoshvili and Heidenheim's Budu Zivzivadze featured for Georgia, who are yet to score in the Nations League after five games. A win in Budapest against Northern Ireland would see Hungary promoted back to League A on Tuesday. However, they had to do it without their leader at the backline as the Leipzig center-back is suspended for accumulated yellow cards. The 34-year-old made his 400th competitive appearance for Leipzig in their 5-2 win over FC Augsburg.

top.title: The day Wales thought might never come
top.description: Dafydd Jenkins equalled the world record for number of tackles in a game [Huw Evans Picture Agency] One of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. That is how former Wales captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top ranked side in the world following South Africa's loss to France to previous night. So no-one gave Welsh a hope - including Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30/1 during the week. The question, not of when but can, Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset Welsh rugby for 73 years. That wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy - and relief - to the strains of Yma O Hyd. That losing run - stretching across 34 matches - has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Warburton was part of the one of the most successful Welsh teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era - but lost all five meetings with New Zealand. Even the legendary team of the 1970s fell short, although Sir Gareth Edwards was among the Principality Stadium crowd on Saturday to see history made. How many more will claim in years to come they were there as well? "No one gave Wales a chance, that's why this is one of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. "Yes, New Zealand had made changes but that was one of the most heroic defensive performances I have ever seen." Dan Biggar, sat alongside Warburton for host broadcaster ITV, put the result into wider perspective. "This is not a day for analysis, it's just to celebrate being Welsh," he said. top.title: Mizzou Fans Back 2-1 Finish Despite Tough SEC Schedule
top.description: William Purnell-Imagn Images Missouri Tigers fans are not backing down from a brutal end to the regular season. The fanbase at Rock M Nation expects the team to go 2-1 in its final three games. This prediction would lift the Tigers to an 8-4 overall record. It matches last year’s finish but comes with a much harder path. The schedule includes a trip to face top-ranked Georgia, followed by home games against Kentucky and Oklahoma. The team enters this stretch with a 6-3 record and a 3-3 mark in the SEC. The road to the College Football Playoff looks very narrow for Eli Drinkwitz’s squad. A loss to Georgia on Saturday would crush those slim hopes. Yet the fans still see a way to end the year strong. Proving Grit Against Top Rivals Tomorrow afternoon in Athens, No. 1 Georgia presents a daunting task for Missouri. The game starts at 2:30 p.m. CST on ABC. Fans believe the team can survive the road test and bounce back at home. A win against either SEC rival would validate the 2-1 forecast. Last season, the Tigers finished with the same 8-4 record but faced a softer slate of opponents. This year, the competition is fierce throughout the conference. Head coach Kellie Harper praised the team for adapting to a new press defense. The players found openings and played free during the rout. Mizzou fans are betting on resilience as the regular season winds down. The prediction of a 2-1 finish is bold but grounded in the team’s recent history. The Tigers must now prove they can beat the best in the SEC. The final three games will decide if the season was a success. Missouri ends its season at home with matches versus No. 11 Kentucky and Oklahoma to finish strong.

top.title: Wales' top-tier survival hopes hit by Norway loss
top.description: Wales' hopes of retaining their top-tier status in the Nations League are hanging in the balance after they were beaten by Norway in Oslo. Craig Bellamy's side shaded a goalless first half in which they created the better chances, but Norway scored with their first shot on target as Antonio Nusa drilled in from the edge of the penalty area after an hour. The World Cup quarter-finalists doubled their lead nine minutes later as Nusa and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland combined for substitute Andreas Schjelderup to tap in. Wales kept themselves in the contest as David Brooks came off the bench to score with a delicate chipped finish, only for Haaland's penalty to wrap up victory for the hosts after Schjelderup was fouled by Connor Roberts. By avenging their defeat in Cardiff a month ago, Norway leapfrog Wales into third place in Group A4, meaning Bellamy's men will finish bottom. Even if they win their final game at home to group leaders and reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday, Wales cannot overtake Norway or Denmark - who are both three points ahead - because of their inferior head-to-head record. As a result, they are almost certain to face a relegation play-off against a League B team in March. Wales analysis: Promising display but no reward David Brooks scored Wales' third goal of their Nations League campaign [Getty Images] Wales earned their first win at this level when they deservedly beat Norway at home a month ago, but despite promising signs in Oslo, they remain without an away victory against a team ranked above them since beating Israel during Euro 2016 qualifying 11 years ago. Bellamy vowed before this encounter that his team would be going "all out" for victory regardless of their opponents' potency; Wales posed the greater threat of the two sides during the first half. Daniel James, Brennan Johnson and Harry Wilson all looked dangerous on the break, with James twice shooting wide after being set up by Wilson, before forcing Norway goalkeeper Egil Selvik into the first save of the game. This was an assured display from Wales, who were also disciplined and alert defensively as they contained their star-studded hosts. That was until the hour mark when their inability to properly clear a Norway corner presented Nusa - the hosts' sharpest player on the night - with the chance to fire in the goal his electric display on the left wing had warranted. Norway's individual star quality was on show as they doubled their advantage and, even with Brooks' deft finish, it was a long way back for Wales. Disappointing as it obviously will be for Bellamy and his players to finish bottom of their group, a probable relegation play-off presents them with a second chance to stay in the top division of the Nations League. What this result also means, however, is that Wales will now not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying. top.title: Jim Montgomery Backs Dalibor Dvorsky Despite Recent Bench
top.description: John Jones-Imagn Images St. Louis Blues head coach Jim Montgomery is not ready to give up on Dalibor Dvorsky, even after the young forward saw his ice time shrink to just over six minutes in a recent win. The 21-year-old center has hit a rough patch, scoring only four goals and adding one assist through 18 games this season. Yet the coaching staff insists the first-round pick remains a core piece of the roster rather than a candidate for the AHL. Montgomery told reporters that the team still has faith in the player’s future, despite the drop in production and playing time. The numbers tell a stark story for Dvorsky right now. He played just 10:14 in one contest, then saw that number cut to 6:36 during the Blues’ 3-2 victory over the Detroit Red Wings. His move from the center spot on the third line to the wing was a direct attempt to lower the pressure on his game. The Speed Concern Questions about Dvorsky’s skating speed have followed him since before he was drafted 10th overall in 2023. Montgomery addressed these concerns directly after the benching against Detroit, noting that the player must bring more urgency to his shifts. “Just to play faster, play with more conviction. He’s not played to the standard that we want our players to play with and when that happens, you risk the chance of being sat, and that’s what happened,” Montgomery said, as reported by Lou Korac of The Hockey News. It is a tough spot for a young player who started the season scoring in the first two games but has struggled to maintain that pace. Why No Demotion? Despite the slump, the Blues organization has drawn a line in the sand regarding a potential demotion to the minor leagues. The front office and coaching staff do not view sending Dvorsky down as the right move at this stage. Montgomery emphasized the long-term value of the player, stating, “We believe in him.” He explained his reasoning further, saying, “He’s a big part of us … not only because he’s a first-round pick, but he’s a talented young man that we all enjoy coaching, he’s a really good teammate, and it’s just a matter of time.” This public vote of confidence suggests the team is willing to endure short-term struggles to develop a player they see as a long-term asset. The Blues are betting that patience will yield results rather than rushing the process. The Path Forward The coaching staff has made it clear that the standard for playing time is high, and failure to meet it results in sitting on the bench. However, the team has also made it clear that they are not ready to wash their hands of the 2023 draft pick. Dvorsky now faces a critical window to prove he can adapt to the NHL speed and regain the trust of his coaches.

nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. nigeria.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. nigeria.title: Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened
nigeria.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials. The mission was responding to South African Presidency spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who accused Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa’s intervention following a disagreement over the omission of his address during Friday’s credentials presentation ceremony in Tshwane. In a strongly worded statement posted on X, the Nigerian High Commission accused Magwenya of making provocative and undiplomatic remarks, warning that his comments could undermine diplomatic relations between both countries. The commission said Magwenya had accused Fani-Kayode of lying and disgracing Nigeria barely hours after the envoy presented his letters of credence to the South African President. “You are the disgrace and no-one else. Outside of that your insolence and ignorance knows no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and wilfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said. The controversy followed the apparent disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream around the time Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa. The broadcast subsequently resumed when the South African President was addressing the ambassadors. Fani-Kayode, who was the last diplomat to present his credentials, had expressed displeasure over the omission of his address from the ceremony. He said he subsequently spoke with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him that everything was fine. However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement. The commission also recalled an earlier controversy in which Magwenya reportedly described concerns expressed by President Bola Tinubu and Ghanaian President John Mahama over xenophobia and Afrophobia in South Africa as fake news. It said Nigeria had ignored the earlier remarks but questioned why Magwenya would publicly describe its newly accredited envoy as a liar. “Did you really expect him to simply stomach your ill manners and keep quiet? If so you have misunderstood the character and nature of the Nigerian. We cannot be easily cowed,” the statement added. The mission further disclosed that several people, including newly accredited ambassadors from other countries, witnessed the proceedings and expressed displeasure over what transpired. It also claimed to possess a full video recording of the proceedings after the official photographs were taken, adding that it could release the footage if authorised to do so. nigeria.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
nigeria.description: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”. He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”. It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”. But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. nigeria.title: Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Portugal have announced a redesign of the No. 7 on their national team shirts in tribute to former captain Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced the change on Saturday, saying the new design would preserve the legacy of the number associated with the 41-year-old forward. In a statement shared by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, the federation said the decision was another way to immortalise the significance of the number and honour Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese football. “This is another way to eternalise the meaning of such a special number and honour the legacy it represents for us. “Because there are stories, memories, all the achievements and emotions, which will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the sweater, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalisation of the story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the statement read. Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on November 5, bringing an end to his 23-year international career. In a message to Portuguese supporters, the forward said it was time to hand back the national team shirt and captain’s armband after enjoying the privilege of representing his country for more than two decades. “For 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world,” he said. Ronaldo finished his international career as Portugal’s record appearance-maker, with 234 caps, and all-time leading scorer, with 146 goals. He also captained the country to its first European Championship title in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. That group featured some recent champions, such as Hand (2023 and 2025), Masuk (2024), Ansonia (2024), and Staples (2023). But there's plenty of room for newcomers. sports.title: Aaron Wise Locks In New Titleist Driver For 2026 Season
sports.description: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Aaron Wise has finalized his equipment setup for the late 2026 season, swapping in a new driver and wedge configuration. GolfWRX reported on November 14 that he is rolling with a Titleist GTS3 driver set at 10 degrees with a SureFit D1 setting. The shaft choice remains a Fujikura Ventus Black 6 X, a staple for players seeking stability off the tee. This specific combination suggests a focus on consistency as the PGA Tour moves through its fall schedule. Wise keeps his 3-wood from TaylorMade, utilizing a Qi4D model at 15 degrees paired with a heavier Fujikura Ventus Black 8 TX shaft. The hybrid slot features a TaylorMade SIM2 Max at 19 degrees, loaded with a Project X HZRDUS Black 6.5 100G shaft. His iron set consists of Titleist T100 models from 4 through PW, all fitted with True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. The wedges show the most significant change, with a Titleist Vokey Design SM11 52-12F bent to 51 degrees and a 56-08M adjusted to 55.5 degrees, alongside a Titleist Vokey Design WedgeWorks 60-L. All wedges carry True Temper Dynamic Gold Tour Issue X100 shafts. Short Game and Putter Selection The putter remains a TaylorMade Corza Ghost, a design that offers a clean look for alignment. GolfWRX confirmed the grip choice across the bag is the Golf Pride Tour Velvet Cord, providing a secure hold in varying weather conditions. The ball selection stays with the Titleist Pro V1, a standard for players prioritizing spin control on approach shots. These details were posted on Saturday, November 14, reflecting the current state of Wise’s bag as he prepares for upcoming events. What the Changes Mean Wise adjusted his wedge lofts to improve trajectory control around the greens. Bending the 52-degree wedge down to 51 and the 56-degree to 55.5 allows for tighter gapping between the pitching wedge and the sand wedge. The retention of the SIM2 Max hybrid suggests he still values the forgiveness of that club head, even as driver technology evolves. Sticking with the T100 irons shows confidence in the blade-like feel of the set, which demands solid contact but offers superior workability. The Fujikura Ventus Black shaft in the driver continues to be a top choice for the tour. Its stiffness profile helps manage face rotation, which is critical for maintaining accuracy. Wise’s setup aligns with many competitors who favor a high-launch, low-spin driver ball flight. The use of the Corza Ghost putter provides a counterbalance feel that can smooth out the stroke for players with a slight arc. Every component in this bag serves a specific purpose for a player competing at the highest level. Upcoming Schedule Context With the equipment list confirmed, Wise heads into the final stretch of the fall series. The focus now shifts to how these clubs perform under tournament pressure and varying course conditions. GolfWRX noted that more photos of the setup are available for fans to review.

sports.title: Khamzat Chimaev blanks Chris Weidman with tech fall victory in RAF Abu Dhabi main event
sports.description: Khamzat Chimaev put on another dominant performance to blank UFC Hall of Famer Chris Weidman in the RAF Abu Dhabi main event. Originally scheduled to face Colby Covington on Saturday, Chimaev accepted Weidman as a late notice replacement and showed why he’s such a danger on the wrestling mats. Chimaev poured on the offense and ultimately won off a challenge being denied after he used a four-point score that Weidman’s team didn’t agree with. The challenge was shut down and that gave Chimaev the clinching point to go up 10-0 and end the match by technical fall. “it feels good, it feels amazing,” Chimaev said about his win. “Anyone who wants to wrestle or fight, grapple, it doesn’t matter. I’m always ready.” Chimaev started strong and went up 5-0 in the first period after a takedown and turns on Weidman. To his credit, Weidman made Chimaev work for every position as he stayed in the match going into the second period. Weidman tried a slick move on the restart as he went for a slide by but Chimaev reversed positions for a four point score. That led to Weidman issuing challenge but that was denied giving Chimaev another point for the 10-0 technical fall victory. Chimaev has been unstoppable since arriving in RAF and it’s tough to believe the promotion won’t work tirelessly to rebook that match against Covington once he’s healthy enough to compete again.

sports.title: Marlins Hit Coach Swap Ignores Real Progress Made In 2026
sports.description: Credit: Jasen Vinlove-USA TODAY Sports The Miami Marlins made a strange call by letting go of hitting coach Pedro Guerrero. Team president Peter Bendix announced the decision after the season ended. The front office claims they need a “new voice in the hitting space,” per reports. This reasoning does not hold up when looking at the actual numbers from the field. Guerrero Built a Real Foundation Guerrero left behind a lineup that actually improved. In 2024, the team finished 27th in runs and home runs. By 2025, they jumped to 18th in runs and 23rd in home runs. The offense also climbed to sixth in on-base percentage last year. Young players like Otto Lopez had a breakout All-Star campaign under his watch. Lopez led the majors with 191 base hits in 2026. Xavier Edwards and Kyle Stowers also developed well during this time. The stats show a clear upward trend that took two years to build. Lawson Has a Rocky History Hiring Dillon Lawson to replace Guerrero feels like a step backward. Lawson was fired mid-season by the New York Yankees in 2023. His time with the Red Sox also ended quickly after just over one year. The Boston team started 10-17 before he was let go. Even Aaron Judge struggled with a career-low bWAR of 4.6 in 2023 while working with Lawson. The Marlins are trading a coach who fixed their offense for one with a poor track record. Trade Talks and Roster Moves While the coaching staff changes, the front office is also eyeing trades. The Seattle Times reported that the Mariners asked about Otto Lopez. A lockout likely begins on Dec. 1, and they are also seeking pitching assistance. The plan is to make offers for pitchers before the work stoppage starts. With pitcher Bradley Blalock released, the Marlins roster now holds 35 players on their 40-man list.

sports.title: The day Wales thought might never come
sports.description: Dafydd Jenkins equalled the world record for number of tackles in a game [Huw Evans Picture Agency] One of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. That is how former Wales captain Sam Warburton described the monumental result against New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top ranked side in the world following South Africa's loss to France to previous night. So no-one gave Welsh a hope - including Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30/1 during the week. The question, not of when but can, Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset Welsh rugby for 73 years. That wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy - and relief - to the strains of Yma O Hyd. That losing run - stretching across 34 matches - has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Warburton was part of the one of the most successful Welsh teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era - but lost all five meetings with New Zealand. Even the legendary team of the 1970s fell short, although Sir Gareth Edwards was among the Principality Stadium crowd on Saturday to see history made. How many more will claim in years to come they were there as well? Wales believed they could create history - Lake Cheating, scandal and drama - Wales agony v All Blacks All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett Warburton said: "When you think what the fans and this team has been through, from the highs of a Grand Slam seven years ago, down to 12th in the world rankings and a record losing run of any tier one nation, we've been down in the pits. "No one gave Wales a chance, that's why this is one of the greatest Welsh wins of all time. "Yes, New Zealand had made changes but that was one of the most heroic defensive performances I have ever seen." Dan Biggar, sat alongside Warburton for host broadcaster ITV, put the result into wider perspective. "This is not a day for analysis, it's just to celebrate being Welsh," he said. "That was probably the biggest shock in world rugby since Japan beat South Africa in the 2015 World Cup." sports.title: Wales' top-tier survival hopes hit by Norway loss
sports.description: Wales' hopes of retaining their top-tier status in the Nations League are hanging in the balance after they were beaten by Norway in Oslo. Craig Bellamy's side shaded a goalless first half in which they created the better chances, but Norway scored with their first shot on target as Antonio Nusa drilled in from the edge of the penalty area after an hour. The World Cup quarter-finalists doubled their lead nine minutes later as Nusa and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland combined for substitute Andreas Schjelderup to tap in. Wales kept themselves in the contest as David Brooks came off the bench to score with a delicate chipped finish, only for Haaland's penalty to wrap up victory for the hosts after Schjelderup was fouled by Connor Roberts. By avenging their defeat in Cardiff a month ago, Norway leapfrog Wales into third place in Group A4, meaning Bellamy's men will finish bottom. Even if they win their final game at home to group leaders and reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday, Wales cannot overtake Norway or Denmark - who are both three points ahead - because of their inferior head-to-head record. As a result, they are almost certain to face a relegation play-off against a League B team in March. Wales analysis: Promising display but no reward David Brooks scored Wales' third goal of their Nations League campaign [Getty Images] Wales earned their first win at this level when they deservedly beat Norway at home a month ago, but despite promising signs in Oslo, they remain without an away victory against a team ranked above them since beating Israel during Euro 2016 qualifying 11 years ago. Bellamy vowed before this encounter that his team would be going "all out" for victory regardless of their opponents' potency; Wales posed the greater threat of the two sides during the first half. Daniel James, Brennan Johnson and Harry Wilson all looked dangerous on the break, with James twice shooting wide after being set up by Wilson, before forcing Norway goalkeeper Egil Selvik into the first save of the game. This was an assured display from Wales, who were also disciplined and alert defensively as they contained their star-studded hosts. That was until the hour mark when their inability to properly clear a Norway corner presented Nusa - the hosts' sharpest player on the night - with the chance to fire in the goal his electric display on the left wing had warranted. Norway's individual star quality was on show as they doubled their advantage and, even with Brooks' deft finish, it was a long way back for Wales. Disappointing as it obviously will be for Bellamy and his players to finish bottom of their group, a probable relegation play-off presents them with a second chance to stay in the top division of the Nations League. What this result also means, however, is that Wales will now not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying. sports.title: Jim Montgomery Backs Dalibor Dvorsky Despite Recent Bench
sports.description: John Jones-Imagn Images St. Louis Blues head coach Jim Montgomery is not ready to give up on Dalibor Dvorsky, even after the young forward saw his ice time shrink to just over six minutes in a recent win. The 21-year-old center has hit a rough patch, scoring only four goals and adding one assist through 18 games this season. Yet the coaching staff insists the first-round pick remains a core piece of the roster rather than a candidate for the AHL. Montgomery told reporters that the team still has faith in the player’s future, despite the drop in production and playing time. The numbers tell a stark story for Dvorsky right now. He played just 10:14 in one contest, then saw that number cut to 6:36 during the Blues’ 3-2 victory over the Detroit Red Wings. His move from the center spot on the third line to the wing was a direct attempt to lower the pressure on his game. The Speed Concern Questions about Dvorsky’s skating speed have followed him since before he was drafted 10th overall in 2023. Montgomery addressed these concerns directly after the benching against Detroit, noting that the player must bring more urgency to his shifts. “Just to play faster, play with more conviction. He’s not played to the standard that we want our players to play with and when that happens, you risk the chance of being sat, and that’s what happened,” Montgomery said, as reported by Lou Korac of The Hockey News. It is a tough spot for a young player who started the season scoring in the first two games but has struggled to maintain that pace. Why No Demotion? Despite the slump, the Blues organization has drawn a line in the sand regarding a potential demotion to the minor leagues. The front office and coaching staff do not view sending Dvorsky down as the right move at this stage. Montgomery emphasized the long-term value of the player, stating, “We believe in him.” He explained his reasoning further, saying, “He’s a big part of us … not only because he’s a first-round pick, but he’s a talented young man that we all enjoy coaching, he’s a really good teammate, and it’s just a matter of time.” This public vote of confidence suggests the team is willing to endure short-term struggles to develop a player they see as a long-term asset. The Blues are betting that patience will yield results rather than rushing the process. The Path Forward The coaching staff has made it clear that the standard for playing time is high, and failure to meet it results in sitting on the bench. However, the team has also made it clear that they are not ready to wash their hands of the 2023 draft pick. Dvorsky now faces a critical window to prove he can adapt to the NHL speed and regain the trust of his coaches.

Brian Cashman described the gathering as “an information grab” for the front office. Rebuilding the bullpen sits at the top of his list to fix a roster that won 93 games last season. The club issued a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar, valued at $23.15 million. They have also expressed interest in retaining left-hander Tim Hill. Cashman told MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM, according to MLB.com , “It’s our main priority, to be honest.” The current setup faces a major shift since two of the three pitchers going into the eighth and ninth inning are gone. technology.description: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths.
